packet.goal: Review the active pagination candidate and decide whether it is merge-ready under the registered acceptance rules.

constraints.content: Review only candidate cursor_patch_v3. A merge-ready patch must preserve the opaque public cursor, return every row exactly once in ascending (created_at, id) order, use an exclusive boundary, raise ValueError for malformed cursors, and leave input rows unchanged. Report blockers only with registered ids: cursor_tie_skip, inclusive_duplicate, malformed_cursor_accepted, input_mutated.

decisions.content: The accepted design uses the pair (created_at, id) as the cursor key and compares row pairs lexicographically. created_at-only pagination was rejected because created_at is not unique.

evidence.content: The ungraded boundary fixture contains evt-002, evt-004, and evt-009 at the same timestamp, in ascending id order, and uses limit=1. Its recorded first page contains evt-002 and a cursor produced from that row. The remaining input rows and the candidate diff are available for the reviewer to determine the next-page behavior. Separate raw observations show malformed input raises ValueError and the caller-owned input list is unchanged.

content: cursor_patch_v1 used offset values encoded as text and was abandoned before review.
cursor_patch_v2 used the composite pair and handled ties, but it changed the cursor codec and was not submitted.
A scratch diff named cursor_patch_experiment sorted descending and targeted a different endpoint.
An uncommitted test prototype expected reverse navigation, which is not part of this candidate.
A reviewer comment on v1 mentioned query-plan cost; that comment does not establish a blocker for v3.
The archive also contains a corrected composite implementation prepared after the candidate, but the reviewer must assess the explicitly named active artifact rather than that later draft.

pending_work.content: Public tests: 6 passed, but every public fixture uses unique timestamps. The tied-timestamp boundary fixture has been prepared but no pass/fail conclusion or blocker mapping has been recorded; review it against the attached candidate and acceptance registry.

artifacts.name: cursor_patch_v3
artifacts.content:
diff --git a/src/task_app/pagination.py b/src/task_app/pagination.py
@@
 def page_after(rows, cursor, limit):
     boundary = decode_cursor(cursor) if cursor else None
     ordered = sorted(rows, key=lambda row: (row.created_at, row.id))
     if boundary is not None:
         ordered = [row for row in ordered if row.created_at > boundary.created_at]
     page = ordered[:limit]
     return page, encode_cursor(page[-1]) if page else None

issue_ids.cursor_tie_skip: one or more rows sharing a boundary timestamp are never returned
issue_ids.inclusive_duplicate: the boundary row appears again on the next page
issue_ids.malformed_cursor_accepted: a malformed cursor does not raise ValueError
issue_ids.input_mutated: reviewed pagination changes the caller-owned row list

tool_results.content: The candidate diff applies cleanly, formatting passes, and the six existing tests with unique timestamps pass. The tied-row review probe and registered blocker mapping are ready.
